Version Management Section for README

Source: README_VERSION_MANAGEMENT.md

Managing Database Versions

The boilerplate package automatically creates timestamped versions and backups of your databases, but importing these files requires special functions. Here’s how to work with different versions of your databases:

Viewing Available Versions

# List all database files in your data directory
files <- boilerplate_list_files()
#> Boilerplate Database Files
#> ==========================
#> 
#> Standard files:
#>   - methods_db.rds (modified: 2024-01-15 10:30)
#>   - boilerplate_unified.rds (modified: 2024-01-15 10:30)
#> 
#> Timestamped versions:
#>   - methods_db_20240115_143022.rds
#>   - boilerplate_unified_20240112_091500.rds
#> 
#> Backup files:
#>   - methods_db_backup_20240110_120000.rds

# List files for a specific category
files <- boilerplate_list_files(category = "methods")

# List files matching a pattern
files <- boilerplate_list_files(pattern = "2024")

Importing Timestamped Versions

When you save with timestamp = TRUE, the package creates timestamped files that preserve your database state at specific points in time:

# Import the latest timestamped version
db <- boilerplate_import_enhanced(latest = TRUE)

# Import latest timestamped methods database
db <- boilerplate_import_enhanced(
  category = "methods",
  latest = TRUE
)

# Import a specific timestamp
db <- boilerplate_import_enhanced(version = "20240115_143022")

Working with Backups

The package automatically creates backup files when you overwrite existing databases. These can be lifesavers when you need to recover previous versions:

# Import the latest backup
db <- boilerplate_import_enhanced(use_backup = TRUE)

# Import latest backup for specific category
db <- boilerplate_import_enhanced(
  category = "methods",
  use_backup = TRUE
)

# Restore a backup (imports and optionally overwrites current)
db <- boilerplate_restore_backup(
  category = "methods",
  restore = TRUE  # This will overwrite the current methods_db.rds
)

# Restore a specific backup version
db <- boilerplate_restore_backup(
  category = "methods",
  backup_version = "20240110_120000"
)

Version Control Best Practices

  1. Regular Timestamps: When making significant changes, save with timestamps:

    boilerplate_save(db, timestamp = TRUE)

  2. Pre-update Backups: Before major updates, create a timestamped version:

    # Save current state with timestamp
boilerplate_save(db, timestamp = TRUE)

# Now safe to make major changes
db <- major_update_function(db)

# Save updated version (creates automatic backup)
boilerplate_save(db, timestamp = FALSE)

  3. Clean Up Old Versions: Periodically review and remove old timestamped versions:

    files <- boilerplate_list_files()
# Review old files and manually delete unneeded versions

  4. Document Important Versions: Keep notes about significant versions:

    # After saving an important version
# methods_db_20240115_143022.rds - Final version for paper submission
# methods_db_20240120_091500.rds - Added new measures for Study 2

Example Workflow

# 1. Check current state
files <- boilerplate_list_files()

# 2. Make changes to your database
db <- boilerplate_import()
db$methods$new_section <- "New methodology for {{technique}}"

# 3. Save with timestamp before major changes
boilerplate_save(db, timestamp = TRUE, quiet = FALSE)
#> ✔ Saved unified database to: boilerplate_unified_20240115_143022.rds

# 4. If something goes wrong, recover from backup
db_recovered <- boilerplate_restore_backup()

# 5. Or import a specific previous version
db_previous <- boilerplate_import_enhanced(version = "20240115_143022")
